newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tutu successor as archbishop installed in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Tutu successor as archbishop installed in S.Africa.

text.p: A little-known bishop was installed on Saturday as Anglican Archbishop for southern Africa, succeeding Desmond Tutu who held the job for 10 years and used his pulpit to preach against apartheid.
Archbishop Winston Ndungane's vast diocese covers South Africa, Mozambique, Namibia, Swaziland, Lesotho and the island of St Helena.
Ndungane studied at London's King College and was formerly the bishop of the diocese covering the historic diamond town of Kimberley.

He led communion immediately after his enthronement at Cape Town's St George's Cathedral, and told national radio he would deliver his first full service as archbishop at the St Mary's Church in the nearby Guguletu black township on Sunday.

When his selection was announced in June, Ndungane said he was overwhelmed by the confidence the church had placed in him, adding: "It is a distinctive honour for me to have been chosen to succeed Archbishop Desmond Tutu, an outstanding church leader of our time."
He said the church's immediate role would be to help heal the wounds inflicted by South Africa's past apartheid policies.
Tutu now heads the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which is seeking to heal old wounds by probing human rights abuses committed over almost three decades of white rule.
